Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaHealth Hospitals third quarter 2025 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. If you are using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaHealth Hospitals' financial results for the third quarter of fiscal 2025. Joining me on the call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Mark Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; and Sarah Jenkins, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Our integrated network of 45 acute care hospitals, 120 outpatient surgery centers, and post-acute facilities across the Southeast and Midwest continues to position us strongly amid industry challenges. We've seen robust growth in high-acuity ortho and neuro cases, expanded ASCs in key markets like Atlanta and Charlotte, and advanced initiatives in telehealth and supply chain optimization. Today, I'll provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, with a spotlight on our progress in operating margin trajectory, the tangible impacts from our cost reduction initiatives, our management of supply costs and other operating expenses, and the contributions from recent acquisitions that are already reshaping our footprint.

These efforts have not only driven top-line momentum but also fortified our margins through disciplined execution on workforce optimization, clinical standardization, and strategic procurement. Now, I'll turn the call over to Mark Thompson to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Mark Thompson:
Thank you, Elena. Good morning, everyone. As Elena mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $1.75 billion, an increase of 15% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, improved payer mix, and contributions from our recent acquisitions.

Our operating expenses were $1.45 billion, representing 82.8% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives like digital transformation and capacity expansion.

Net income for the quarter was $210 million, or $1.48 per diluted share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Let me now dive deeper into these results and provide color on the areas Elena highlighted, starting with our outlook for operating margins, which remain a cornerstone of our disciplined financial strategy here at NovaHealth Hospitals. Our network positions us well to navigate headwinds like persistent reimbursement pressures from CMS's upcoming 2.9% cut to inpatient prospective payment system rates for FY 2026 and elevated labor costs amid the ongoing RN shortage.

For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, we are guiding to an operating margin in the range of 10.5% to 11.5%, representing a 150 to 250 basis point improvement sequentially from Q3's 9.0% and roughly flat year-over-year after adjusting for the one-time $25 million Medicare sequestration clawback we absorbed last Q4. This guidance embeds same-facility revenue growth of 5.0% to 6.0%, driven by a 3% increase in admissions—primarily in high-acuity ortho and neuro cases—and 4% outpatient volume growth, bolstered by our expansion of ASCs in high-growth MSAs like Atlanta and Charlotte.

On the cost side, we expect adjusted admissions per occupied bed to hold steady at 4.8, with case mix index climbing to 1.82 from 1.79, reflecting our focus on elective procedures. Labor costs, which comprise 55% of our total OpEx, should moderate to a 3.5% year-over-year increase after our Q3 success in backfilling 85% of open RN positions through our partnership with AMN Healthcare and our proprietary Travel Nurse Optimization Program. This program has reduced agency spend by 22% YTD, bringing it down to 8% of total nursing payroll from 12% a year ago.

Supply chain initiatives will be a key margin tailwind, with our Group Purchasing Organization collaboration—modeled after Vizient's supply chain playbook—delivering another 50 to 75 basis points of savings through consolidated pharma contracts for high-cost biologics like Keytruda and Ozempic analogs, which now account for 15% of our drug spend. We've also rolled out RFID-enabled inventory management across 80% of our facilities, cutting supply waste by 11% and positioning us ahead of peers like HCA Healthcare, who are just now piloting similar tech.

Regionally, our Southeast cluster—representing 60% of EBITDA—should see margins expand to 12.5%, fueled by robust commercial volumes from Blue Cross Blue Shield of Georgia's value-based care pilots, where we're targeting 25% of ortho DRGs under bundled payments by year-end. In contrast, our Midwest markets face softer Medicare mix at 52% of payer revenues versus 48% nationally, capping margins there at 8.5%, but we're mitigating this with a $50 million investment in tele-stroke and tele-ICU hubs to boost utilization 10% in rural Iowa and Illinois facilities.

Looking further out to full-year FY 2026, we anticipate operating margins of 11.0% to 12.0%, up from an implied 10.2% in FY 2025. This reflects sustained revenue per admission growth of 4.5%, anchored by our shift to site-neutral reimbursements and outpatient migration—outpatient now 58% of total volumes, in line with Tenet Healthcare's trajectory. Strategic levers include digital transformation with full Epic MyChart rollout by Q2 2026, expected to reduce length-of-stay by 0.5 days and administrative costs by 3%, similar to Community Health Systems' post-Epic gains; payer innovation through negotiating 15 new narrow-network contracts with UnitedHealthcare and Humana, aiming for 200 basis points of reimbursement uplift on commercial lives; capacity expansion by adding 150 licensed beds in Florida and Texas high-growth markets, with ROI modeled at 18% EBITDA margins within 24 months, funded via our $750 million Term Loan B at SOFR+225bps; and ESG-aligned initiatives like our carbon-neutral OR pilot with Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci Xi systems, reducing energy costs 7% while enhancing procedural throughput.

Of course, risks include potential delays in our $120 million in pending state supplemental payments from Florida's Medicaid program and inflationary pressures on medical supplies if steel tariffs escalate. But with $1.2 billion in liquidity and leverage at 3.2x net debt-to-EBITDA—well below our 4.0x covenant—we're positioned to outperform.

Next, I'd like to discuss the impact of our ongoing cost reduction initiatives, which have been a cornerstone of our strategy to drive sustainable margin expansion amid persistent reimbursement pressures from Medicare Advantage plans—where we've seen average reimbursement rates flatline at around 2.5% year-over-year—and inflationary headwinds on labor and supplies. These efforts delivered $285 million in run-rate savings for the full year, exceeding our initial $250 million target by 14%. Sequentially from Q2, we realized an additional $42 million in savings, contributing to a 180-basis-point expansion in our adjusted EBITDA margin to 12.8% for the quarter.

Breaking this down by key pillars: First, workforce optimization accounted for 45% of our total savings, or $128 million annualized. Labor remains our largest expense at 52% of total operating costs, exacerbated by post-COVID nurse shortages. We've reduced agency and contract labor spend by 38% year-over-year, from $210 million in Q3 2024 to $130 million this quarter. This was achieved through AI-driven workforce management platforms—we rolled out ShiftMed's integrated scheduling software across 85% of our 120-hospital footprint, leveraging predictive analytics to match staffing to patient acuity and census patterns, reducing overtime by 22% and improving nurse retention to 89% from 82% a year ago, directly correlating to a 15-basis-point lift in our labor cost per equivalent admission, now at $1,420.

Clinical pathway standardization, partnering with our employed physician groups, implemented evidence-based protocols via our Epic EHR system, shortening average length of stay by 0.4 days to 4.6 days system-wide. This cut nursing hours per patient day by 8% and boosted our case mix index to 1.68, up 2% YoY, helping offset lower acuity volumes. Regionally, this has been most pronounced in our Southeast markets—Florida and Texas—where urban hospitals saw 25% agency reductions versus 15% in rural Midwest facilities.

Second, supply chain and procurement efficiencies delivered $92 million in savings, or 32% of the total. Medical and surgical supplies represent 22% of our cost base, with inflation at 4-6% for orthopedic implants and pharmaceuticals. We've centralized procurement through our Vizient GPO contract, renegotiated for an additional 2.5% in rebates, and shifted 65% of high-volume drugs to biosimilars and generics.

Key wins include a 28% reduction in 340B-eligible drug costs through enhanced contract pharmacy management with Omnicell, saving $45 million. For devices, RFPs with Medtronic and Stryker yielded 12-15% discounts on hip/knee implants tied to volume commitments exceeding 10,000 units annually. Vendor consolidation and just-in-time inventory using RFID tracking and blockchain pilots with GHX cut inventory carrying costs by 18%, from $65 million to $53 million, while reducing stockouts by 40%, critical as payer mix shifts toward commercial HMO plans at 42% of revenues.

In the Northeast, these yielded 35% savings versus 25% in the West, maintaining supply expense per case at $3,200, flat YoY despite 5% volume growth.

Third, technology and operational leverage contributed $45 million or 16% of savings. We're accelerating digital transformation to counter rising SG&A costs, held flat at 8.2% of revenue. Scaling our Teladoc-integrated platform to 95% of sites reduced avoidable ED visits by 12%, translating to 15,000 fewer inpatient days and $22 million in savings. Outpatient shift is key—ambulatory revenues now 38% of total, up from 32%, with margins 500 basis points above inpatient. Post our $150 million Epic MyChart upgrade, denial rates dropped to 4.2% from 7.1%, accelerating days in A/R to 48 from 56. AI tools automated 70% of prior auths, saving 250 FTE equivalents.

Finally, facility and overhead rationalization rounded out at $20 million or 7%. We divested two underperforming rural hospitals in Ohio, generating $75 million in proceeds while exiting $12 million in annual losses, and consolidated back-office functions via RPA bots, cutting admin costs by 14%.

These initiatives are embedded in our High Reliability Organization framework, targeting 15% EBITDA margins by 2026. Amid CMS's 2.9% IPPS cut for FY2025 and MA headwinds—where star ratings drive 85% of our Medicare reimbursements—we're positioning for value-based care, with early wins in bundled payments with UnitedHealthcare showing 8% margin uplift on ortho episodes. Regionally, expect outperformance in Sunbelt markets at 14% margins versus legacy Midwest at 11%, with $100 million in capex redirected to ASCs and micro-hospitals. Risks include RN wage inflation at 4-5% and supply volatility from Red Sea disruptions, but hedging via forward contracts mitigates 70%. These actions have de-risked our model, funding 5% dividend growth and $500 million in buybacks this year.

Turning now to supply costs and other operating expenses, which came in at $1.28 billion for the quarter, up 4.2% year-over-year, or 150 basis points as a percentage of net patient service revenue at 27.8%. This was slightly ahead of our guided range but reflects a resilient operating model amid inflationary pressures and supply chain headwinds challenging the acute care hospital sector.

Supply costs totaled $892 million, representing 70% of the total bucket and 19.4% of revenue—up from 18.7% a year ago. Medical and surgical supplies drove 55%, pharmaceuticals 30%, and implants/devices the balance. Year-over-year, supplies rose 6.1%, outpacing our 3.8% revenue growth, due to pharmaceutical inflation with a 9% increase from shortages in generics like piperacillin-tazobactam and oncology agents like carboplatin, plus 25% surge in GLP-1 agonists like semaglutide in outpatient clinics and bariatrics, adding $12 million. Device and implant costs climbed 7.2%, with hip/knee replacements at $18,500 per case from $17,200 YoY amid raw material hikes, and cath lab stents/TAVR adding $8 million headwind from 15% procedural ramps.

Broader disruptions like 20% higher ocean freight rates hit PPE and IV fluids. Regionally, Southeast supply costs held flat at 18.9% thanks to Vizient GPO renewals locking 5-7% rebates on $250 million in commodities, while Midwest expanded to 20.5% due to IPPS dynamics.

Other operating expenses hit $388 million, up 1.1% YoY and 8.4% of revenue. Utilities rose 4% to $45 million on natural gas volatility and expansions, professional fees up 3% but moderated as travel nurse rates fell 18%.

Our response includes Oracle's AI-powered procurement across 85% of hospitals, achieving 4.2% reduction in supply spend per CMI-adjusted patient day, cutting stockouts 35% and excess inventory 22%, with working capital days in supplies at 28 from 34. Initiatives: GPO leverage and direct contracting expanded to 95% of ortho implants for $25 million savings via DePuy Synthes; standardization of 1,200 SKUs yielding 8-12% savings; regional tailwinds like California Medi-Cal bundles and Texas hub-and-spoke; RFID with Impinj reducing OR waste 15%; ESG shifts qualifying for green rebates.

Looking forward, Q4 supply costs grow 4-5% YoY, moderating to 3.5% FY2025, other op-ex flat to down 1%, positioning for 250-300 bps EBITDA expansion in H2.

Finally, on the transformative impact of our two strategic acquisitions completed earlier this year: the $450 million purchase of Sunbelt Hospital Group in February, adding five acute-care facilities and two freestanding EDs in Florida and Georgia, and the $220 million acquisition of NeuroCare Partners in May, with outpatient neurology, oncology infusion, and 15 ASCs across Texas and the Carolinas. Funded by $300 million in 4.75% senior unsecured notes and $370 million from our revolver, they've been accretive from day one.

Pro forma, consolidated net patient service revenues grew 18% YoY to $1.42 billion in Q3, with acquired assets contributing $285 million or 20%. Organic growth was 7%, from 5% volumes and 2.2% CMI to 1.68. Sunbelt delivered $180 million at 72% occupancy, fueled by Florida's 65+ growth and 12% joint replacement uptick. NeuroCare's $105 million had 92% cash/commercial mix, boosting system payer mix 300 bps and outpatient sequential growth 14%.

EBITDA hit $312 million, up 22% YoY, margins +150 bps to 22.0%. Adjusted for $18 million integration, $32 million run-rate synergies on track for $75 million FY target: 45% from HealthTrust GPO 8-10% discounts; 30% back-office; 25% clinical standardization cutting ALOS 0.4 days to 4.2. Southeast synergies accelerated with 1,200-bed cluster at 15% share, 8% cross-referrals; Texas ASCs drove 11% surgical volumes. Carolinas labor offset by AI scheduling improving retention to 88%, agency -22%.

Balance sheet: net debt $2.8 billion, 3.6x leverage. 15% EPS accretive, adding $0.28 to $1.12 Q3 adjusted EPS. FCF $185 million supported $75 million repurchases. Tech: Epic integration recovered $12 million; tele-neurology at 15,000 visits/month.

Strategically, positions us for hybrid model, targeting 25% revenues from ASCs/outpatient by 2025 at 15-20% margins vs. inpatient 15%. FY acquisition add: $1.1 billion rev, $220 million EBITDA, synergies to $90 million 2026. Raised FY2025 guidance: rev $5.75-5.85B, EBITDA $1.25-1.28B.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Elena.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mark. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of reimbursement pressures from Medicare Advantage and CMS cuts on your operations?

Elena Vasquez:
Good morning, John. Absolutely, and thanks for the question. As Mark detailed, we're navigating these headwinds head-on across our network. The 2.9% IPPS cut for FY2026 and flat MA reimbursements at 2.5% YoY are industry-wide challenges, but our payer innovation— like 15 new narrow-network contracts with UnitedHealthcare and Humana—aims for 200 bps uplift on commercial lives. In value-based care pilots with Blue Cross Blue Shield of Georgia, we're targeting 25% of ortho DRGs under bundles, delivering early 8% margin gains. Our shift to outpatient at 58% of volumes, plus tele-stroke/ICU investments boosting rural utilization 10%, helps offset softer Medicare mix in the Midwest at 52%. Synergies from acquisitions like Sunbelt have improved payer mix 300 bps, reducing exposure. Overall, these position us for the 11-12% FY2026 margin guidance.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. What are your expectations for patient volume growth in the next quarter, considering the current environment?

Mark Thompson:
Thanks, Lisa. Patient volumes remain a bright spot. For Q4, we expect 3% admission growth, focused on high-acuity ortho/neuro, and 4% outpatient, driven by ASC expansions in Atlanta/Charlotte and NeuroCare's infusion/ASC ramp. Same-facility growth 5-6%, with CMI to 1.82. Post-acquisition, Sunbelt's 72% occupancy and 12% elective uptick in Florida, plus cross-referrals, support this. Outpatient migration to 58%, telehealth reducing ED visits 12%, and 150 new beds in FL/TX add capacity. Risks like RN shortages are mitigated by backfilling 85% positions and AI scheduling, holding adjusted admissions per bed at 4.8. We're confident in sustained momentum.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
Good morning, team. On supply chain, how are you thinking about ongoing inflation and disruptions?

Mark Thompson:
Hi Mike. Supply costs up 6.1% YoY to 19.4% of revenue, driven by 9% pharma inflation on GLP-1s and generics shortages, plus 7.2% on implants from raw materials. Freight 20% above 2022 levels post-Red Sea. But our initiatives—Vizient GPO renewals, Oracle AI procurement cutting spend 4.2%, RFID reducing waste 15-22%, and standardization of 1,200 SKUs—are delivering. Biosimilars cover 60% HER2+ regimens, saving 25%; direct contracting 15% on biologics. Regional: Southeast flat at 18.9%, Midwest up but offset by Medline JIT. Q4 growth 4-5%, moderating FY to 3.5%, supporting 250-300 bps margin expansion.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the NovaHealth Hospitals third quarter 2025 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
